values.en: Unit Vector Orthogonal to Its Derivative
values.zh-CN: 单位向量与其导数正交

values.en: If a $C^{1}$ vector-valued function $\gamma\colon(a,b)\to\mathbb{R}^{3}$ has constant norm $1$ on the open interval $(a,b)$ (with $a<b$), that is $\lVert\gamma(t)\rVert\equiv 1$, then its derivative is orthogonal to it: $\gamma'(t)\perp\gamma(t)$, i.e. $\langle\gamma'(t),\gamma(t)\rangle=0$ for every $t\in(a,b)$. Indeed $\lVert\gamma\rVert^{2}=\langle\gamma,\gamma\rangle$ is constant on that interval, so differentiating gives $2\langle\gamma',\gamma\rangle=0$. The hypothesis is a condition on an interval, not at a single point: for $\gamma(t)=(t,1+t)$ one has $\lVert\gamma(0)\rVert=1$ but $\langle\gamma'(0),\gamma(0)\rangle=1\neq 0$, so the single-point assumption does not suffice. Conversely, if $\langle\gamma',\gamma\rangle=0$ throughout an interval, then $\lVert\gamma\rVert$ is constant there (though not necessarily equal to $1$). This is the fact used repeatedly in the sequel: each of $\boldsymbol{t},\boldsymbol{n},\boldsymbol{b}$ is a unit vector field, so each of their derivatives lies in the plane orthogonal to it.
values.zh-CN: 若 $C^{1}$ 向量值函数 $\gamma\colon(a,b)\to\mathbb{R}^{3}$ 在开区间 $(a,b)$（$a<b$）上具有常值范数 $1$，即 $\lVert\gamma(t)\rVert\equiv 1$，则其导数与其正交：$\gamma'(t)\perp\gamma(t)$，即对每个 $t\in(a,b)$ 有 $\langle\gamma'(t),\gamma(t)\rangle=0$。事实上 $\lVert\gamma\rVert^{2}=\langle\gamma,\gamma\rangle$ 在该区间上为常数，求导得 $2\langle\gamma',\gamma\rangle=0$。该假设是区间上的条件，而非单点条件：对 $\gamma(t)=(t,1+t)$ 有 $\lVert\gamma(0)\rVert=1$，但 $\langle\gamma'(0),\gamma(0)\rangle=1\neq 0$，故单点假设不充分。反之，若在区间上处处有 $\langle\gamma',\gamma\rangle=0$，则 $\lVert\gamma\rVert$ 在该区间上为常数（但不必等于 $1$）。这正是后文反复用到的事实：$\boldsymbol{t},\boldsymbol{n},\boldsymbol{b}$ 均为单位向量场，故它们各自的导数都落在与其正交的平面内。
